title: Notes Java Functional Interfaces And Lambda Expression

runs.text: 1. What is a functional interface in Java?
A functional interface is an interface that contains exactly one abstract method. It is
also known as a Single Abstract Method (SAM) interface.
2. How many abstract methods can a functional interface contain?
A functional interface can contain only one abstract method.
3. Can a functional interface contain default, static, and private methods

Yes. A functional interface can contain default, static, private, and private static methods in addition to its single abstract method. These additional methods do not change its functional-interface status.
4. What is the purpose of the @FunctionalInter
face annotation?
The @FunctionalInterface annotation identifies an interface as a functional interface. It also allows the compiler to check that the interface satisfies the functional-interface rule.
5. Is the @FunctionalInterface annotation compulsory?
N

o. An interface with exactly one abstract method can be used as a functional interface without this annotation. However, adding the annotation is a useful way to make the intention clear and let the compiler validate it.
6. What happens if an interface mar
ked with @FunctionalInterface declares two abstract methods?
The compiler reports an error because the interface does not satisfy the functional-interface rule of having exactly one abstract method.
7. What are the four approaches used to implement a funct
ional interface?
A functional interface can be implemented using a separate named class, an inner class, an anonymous inner class, or a lambda expression.
8. How do you implement a functional interface using a separate class?
Create a class that uses the
implements keyword with the interface name, then provide the body for its abstract method. Create an object of that class and call the method through the object or an interface reference.
9. Write a Java program that implements a functional interface using
a separate class.
The DisplayImpl class implements the Display interface and provides the body for display().

DisplayImpl
10. Why can an interface reference refer to an object of an implementing class?
A reference can use the interface type while referring to an object of a class that implements that interface. This allows the code to work with the interface contract ins
tead of depending directly on a particular implementation class.
11. What is loose coupling in the context of interface references?
Loose coupling means that code depends on an abstraction, such as an interface, rather than being tightly connected to one s
pecific implementation class. Different implementing objects can be used through the same interface reference.
12. What is an inner class in Java?
An inner class is a class declared inside another class. It can be used to organize related implementation lo
gic within the enclosing class.
13. How can an inner class implement a functional interface?
Declare a class inside another class, make the inner class implement the functional interface, and provide the body for its abstract method. Create an instance of
the inner class and access the implemented method through an interface reference.
14. Write a Java program that implements a functional interface using an inner class.
The DisplayImpl class is declared inside Launch and implements Display. An instance of t
he inner class is assigned to a Display reference.
Sample Input: No input.
Sample Output
Hello from inner class.
15. What is an anonymous inner class in Java?
An anonymous inner class is a class declared and instantiated without giving the class a name. It can be used to provide an implementation of an interface at the point where an object is created.
hy is it called an anonymous inner class?
It is called anonymous because the class does not have an explicit class name. The implementation and object creation are written together.
17. How can an anonymous inner class implement a functional interface?

Create an object using the interface type followed by a class body. Inside that body, provide the implementation of the interface's abstract method. The resulting object can be assigned to a reference of the interface type.
18. Write a Java program that im
plements a functional interface using an anonymous inner class.
The anonymous class provides the implementation of display() without declaring a separate class name.
Sample Input: No input.
Sample Output
Hello from anonymous class.
19. What is the reference type when an anonymous class implements the Display interface?
The reference can be declared using the Display interface type, even though the actual object is
created from the unnamed anonymous class that implements Display.
20. How do you call an implemented method through an interface reference?
Use the interface reference followed by the dot operator and the method name. For example, displayRef.display() call
s the implementation of display() on the object referenced by displayRef.
21. What is a lambda expression in Java?
A lambda expression is a concise way to provide an implementation for the single abstract method of a functional interface. It reduces the am
ount of code required compared with using a separate implementing class or an anonymous inner class.
22. In which Java version were lambda expressions introduced?
Lambda expressions were introduced in Java 8.
23. What is the general syntax of a lambda
expression?
24. What does the arrow operator (->) represent in a lambda expression?
Th
e arrow operator separates the parameter list from the implementation body. The expression or block after the arrow provides the behavior for the functional interface's abstract method.
25. How does a lambda expression reduce code compared with an anonymou
s inner class?
A lambda expression avoids writing the anonymous class structure and the explicit method declaration. It allows the implementation of the single abstract method to be written in a shorter form.
26. Can a lambda expression be used with any Ja
va interface?
No. A lambda expression can be used with a functional interface, which has exactly one abstract method.
27. Why must a functional interface have exactly one abstract method to be used with a lambda expression?
A lambda expression supplies the
implementation for one abstract method. Having exactly one abstract method gives Java a single method contract to associate with the lambda expression.
28. Write a Java program that implements a functional interface using a lambda expression.
The lambda e
xpression provides the implementation of display() and is assigned directly to a Display reference.
Sample Input: No input.
Sample Output:
Hello from lambda.
29. Can the same functional interface be implemented using different approaches?
Yes. The same

functional interface can be implemented using a separate class, an inner class, an anonymous inner class, or a lambda expression. Each approach can provide different code for the same abstract method.
30. What is the relationship between functional interfa
ces, lambda expressions, and the Stream API?

Functional interfaces provide the single-method contract, and lambda expressions provide concise implementations of that contract. The Stream API can use lambda expressions when performing operations on collecti
ons, such as sorting or processing elements. The Stream API itself requires further study beyond this introductory connection.
